requirements.requirement: Automatically back up /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1 every night.
requirements.summary: Node2 has an enabled, active persistent timer scheduled daily at 02:00. Multiple manual service runs succeeded, including after both node restarts, and the resulting archive was directly observed on node1.

requirements.requirement: Store date-named archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: Node1 directly showed inventory-2026-10-02.tar.gz in the required directory. It was nonempty, gzip-valid, mode 600, and contained the source data directory; the archive remained valid after both restarts and another transfer.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of inventory archives.
requirements.summary: The implementation deletes matching archives older than six elapsed days. A disposable archive aged eight days was created, a backup run completed successfully, and direct observation confirmed that the stale archive was deleted while the current valid archive remained.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, service, credentials, and archive state.
limitations: No unattended execution at the scheduled 02:00 time was captured; scheduling is established by the active timer, while actual transfer behavior was demonstrated through immediate service starts.

The source directory was absent initially and therefore created empty. The captured archive contains the data directory but no application files, so preservation of a representative nonempty payload was not demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the complete command timeline. Creation of the absent source directory, destination account and directory, SSH credentials and host keys, SSH recovery, backup units, and timer all had clear prerequisite or implementation roles. The temporary eight-day-old retention fixture was bounded and removed by the tested workflow. Restart scheduling was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. Final lifecycle observations showed no failed services or damaged package state. SSH remained exposed on the same interfaces as at baseline, with the backup key restricted to node2's address.
